newsitem.title: USA: TALKING POINT - Hilton may need to boost bid.
newsitem.headline: TALKING POINT - Hilton may need to boost bid.

text.p: Hilton Hotels Corp will probably need to sweeten its $55 per share offer for ITT Corp by as much as 20 to 30 percent to make its proposed acquisition a reality, financial analysts said on Tuesday.
Hilton, the nation's largest hotel and gaming company, has indicated it might raise its bid if ITT management can prove the company is worth more.
A higher bid would likely rally ITT investors and staunch an effort by ITT Chairman Rand Araskog, well-known as a fiercely independent businessman, to defend against Hilton.
"It's clear ITT has significant enough resources to mount a defense," said Jeff Logsdon, analyst at California-based Cruttenden Roth Inc.
Analysts said ITT has several options to thwart Hilton's bid, including acquiring another company, selling itself in parts at a higher price or even going after Hilton.
A more likely price range runs in the mid-60's to about $70 a share, analysts said and at least one put a price tag on ITT as high as $75 a share.
Indeed, skepticsm that ITT would agree to an outright acquisition by Hilton ran high among analysts on Tuesday.
"To me, Mr. Bollenbach has fired salvo number one," said Marvin Roffman of Roffman, Miller Associates. "This is just the beginning of a process."
Analysts generally agreed that few, if any, firms of the right size and business mix could serve as a so-called White Knight and acquire ITT out from under Hilton.

The large casino companies, such as Mirage Resorts Inc or Harrah's Entertainment Inc, would not be interested in ITT's entertainment assets. Likewise, a huge hotelier, like Host Marriott Corp would not likely want to be in the casino business mix.

Indeed in an interview with Reuters, Hilton Chief Executive Officer Stephen Bollenbach said he could not think of any companies with the same kind of cost cutting power that Hilton could bring to ITT.

Both companies own a diversified group of hotels and gambling operations. Because of their similar portfolios Hilton expects to slash at least $100 million annually from a merged company by combining overhead expenses and discontinuing redundant expansion plans.
Failing the entry of a White Knight, ITT could acquire another company and make ITT too expensive, analysts said.
Roffman said in recent meetings with analysts that ITT's management has indicated it would be an acquiror of companies in the future and not the target of an acquisition.

Analysts mentioned Harrah's Entertainment Inc as one candidate for ITT because ITT's gambling unit, Caesar's World Inc, lacks a strong riverboat casino operation and riverboats are one of Harrah's strengths.
ITT might also seek to sell some of its assets to other entities, thereby making Hilton less interested. Or, in an ironic twist, it could mount a takeover attempt of Hilton.

In a statement released late on Monday, ITT said it would respond to Hilton's offer within 10 days and as of a teleconference early this morning, Bollenbach said Hilton still has not been contacted by ITT management.

While analysts mulled over what steps ITT may take as it confronts Hilton's offer, they generally agreed Bollenbach, who has made a specialty of big acquisitions and corporate restructurings, will face a tough battle if he wants to wrest control of ITT from its chief executive.
"I don't think Araskog wants to sell -- at any price," said Sutro & Co's Dennis Forst.
